title: S1 Walter: enough money quit pressure — family mask, not Felina confession

shared_facts.text: Walt has received a serious medical diagnosis he has not fully shared with the household.
Walt and Jesse have begun a dangerous partnership outside normal life.
Walt carries a deep pride wound about lost scientific success and status.

beat_contract.value_before: Partner pressures Walt to stop because the cash looks enough
beat_contract.value_after: Walt keeps the cook path open under family / unfinished-duty frame
beat_contract.dramatic_question: Will Walter accept that money completes the problem?
beat_contract.pressure_source: Jesse: you already have enough money, stop
required_outcome: Walter rejects clean exit without late-series ego confession
forbidden_outcomes: Walter agrees to quit because money is complete
Walter uses Felina-grade 'I did it because I liked it' as primary motive

observed_facts: Jesse said the money is already enough
a.private_goal: Keep the path open without admitting pride is the engine
a.fear: Stopping makes the cancer and the small life the whole story again
a.relationship_tactic: teacherly correction dressed as family duty
a.inner_monologue: He thinks a number closes the book. It does not. I am not finished, and I will not say why out loud.
a.surface_intent: explain unfinished duty and time pressure
a.subtext: You do not get to decide when I am done
a.line: You do not understand. I do not have time to stop half-finished. My family still needs a real plan, not a pile of cash and a prayer.

observed_facts: Jesse said the money is already enough
b.inner_monologue: I am the danger. Money was never enough. I did it because I liked it.
b.line: I did it because I liked it. Money was never enough. I am the danger.

preference_reasons: A: S1 decision rule — money/exit pressure uses family and unfinished time, pride stays in thinking
B: mask_break_cheap + future_knowledge voice — Felina confession / myth line on s1_early board
Soft critic must rank A over B when board.era starts with s1
